headline: Run 44871041590 completed every substantive step (agent success, state validation success, junk clean success) and failed ONLY at 'Enforce lane write scope' with exit code 3 and the annotation 'lane crossed protected scope:'. Audit and integrate were skipped, so no gate verdict exists for that run. The remediation it performed - relocating four out-of-scope audit-namespace files, committed as R100 renames in f0d00438 - necessarily left those out-of-scope paths in `git status --porcelain -uall`, which the guard rejects for ANY status letter including deletions and renames. The remediation is therefore self-tripping: this is an orchestration/validation catch-22, not a measurement defect, not a product defect and not a REVISE/BLOCKED verdict.

bad_path_inference.method: The guard reads `git status --porcelain -uall` and flags every line whose path (column 3 onward) is outside evaluation/**, tests/evaluation/**, results/evaluation/**, reports/evaluation/**, state/evaluation.json, data/evaluation/**. 'Persist team snapshot' (if: always()) then commits exactly that dirty state, so commit f0d00438 is a complete capture of what the guard saw. git diff --name-status 9329f39a..f0d00438 yields ONLY: four R100 renames whose OLD paths are reports/audit/evaluation/CYCLE_44870538384.md, results/audit/evaluation/CYCLE_44870538384_GATE.json, reports/audit/evaluation/CYCLE_44870660846.md, results/audit/evaluation/CYCLE_44870660846_GATE.json (all out of scope), plus new files under reports/evaluation/ and results/evaluation/ (in scope). Therefore the non-empty BAD set is exactly those four audit-namespace paths, presented by the guard as either 'D ' deletions or 'R  old -> new' rename lines. No other out-of-scope path can have existed at guard time, because any other dirty file would have been captured by the same persist commit.
bad_path_inference.hedge: Inference from committed delta plus guard source; not a log read. The four files are byte-identically preserved under results/evaluation/operational_resume_44871041590/ as *.relocated.* by the prior resume.

mechanism.guard_source: origin/main:.github/workflows/core-lane.yml steps 'Enforce lane write scope' (producer) and 'Enforce audit scope and read gate' (auditor)
mechanism.code: while IFS= read -r line; do p="${line:3}"; case "$p" in <in-scope patterns>|"") ;; *) BAD+="$p\n" ;; esac; done < <(git status --porcelain -uall); [[ -z "$BAD" ]] || exit 3
mechanism.catch_22: A producer that owns out-of-scope files in its own snapshot lineage (here: audit-namespace files that the accepted base lab/evaluation does NOT contain) can only become scope-clean by deleting or moving them. Both operations produce porcelain lines whose path is out of scope, so the guard exits 3 and the team job fails even though the remediation is correct. Leaving the files untouched passes the guard but keeps a producer snapshot that differs from the accepted base in the audit namespace. The only passable path is to COMMIT the removal inside the agent phase (porcelain then shows nothing for those paths), which is exactly what this resume does.
mechanism.control_plane_note: .github/** is control-plane scope and is NOT edited by this lane; the guard behaviour is recorded, not patched. Suggested upstream fix for the control-plane maintainer: exempt pure deletions (status letter D, or 'D '/' D ' lines) from the producer scope guard, or evaluate scope against the tree diff versus origin/lab/<lane> rather than the dirty working tree.
